pharm: Selective aldosterone receptor antagonist; potassium-sparing antihypertensive
quick: HFrEF post-MI: start 25 mg once daily, titrate to 50 mg once daily within 4 weeks. Hypertension: 50 mg once daily (up to 50 mg twice daily)
May take with or without food
Data insufficient; use only if clearly needed
Unknown if excreted in human milk; weigh benefit/risk
Contraindicated if CrCl <=30 mL/min; for HTN contraindicated if CrCl <50 mL/min or creatinine elevated
No adjustment in mild-moderate impairment; not studied in severe
No specific interaction; additive hypotension possible
Serum potassium (before, within first week, at 1 month, then periodically) and renal function
summary: Eplerenone is a selective mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist used to improve survival after acute MI in patients with HFrEF, and to treat hypertension. Its key risk is hyperkalemia, especially with renal impairment, diabetes, or concomitant RAAS blockers/NSAIDs/strong CYP3A inhibitors, mandating potassium monitoring.
indications: Improving survival of stable adults with symptomatic HFrEF after acute MI

dosage.t: Titrate to target 50 mg once daily within 4 weeks as tolerated
dosage.n: Adjust by serum potassium per label table; measure K+ before starting

dosage.t: If inadequate response, increase to 50 mg twice daily
dosage.n: Higher doses not recommended (no added efficacy, more hyperkalemia)

admin: Measure serum potassium before initiation and periodically thereafter
Titrate based on potassium levels per the label dosing table
moa: Eplerenone binds selectively to the mineralocorticoid receptor and blocks the binding of aldosterone, a component of the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS), reducing sodium/water retention and the deleterious cardiovascular/renal effects of aldosterone.

absolute: Concomitant strong CYP3A inhibitors (ketoconazole, itraconazole, nefazodone, troleandomycin, clarithromycin, ritonavir, nelfinavir)
For hypertension: type 2 diabetes with microalbuminuria; serum creatinine >2.0 mg/dL (men) or >1.8 mg/dL (women); CrCl <50 mL/min; or concomitant potassium supplements/potassium-sparing diuretics
relative: Concomitant ACE inhibitors, ARBs, NSAIDs, moderate CYP3A inhibitors

preg: Available human data are insufficient to establish a drug-associated risk. Use during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk.
lact: It is not known whether eplerenone is excreted in human milk. Consider benefits of breastfeeding against potential risk.
renal: Contraindicated if CrCl <=30 mL/min. Increased hyperkalemia risk with impaired renal function; for hypertension contraindicated below CrCl 50 mL/min or with elevated creatinine. Monitor potassium and renal function closely.
hepatic: No dose adjustment in mild-to-moderate hepatic impairment; use in severe hepatic impairment has not been evaluated.

major: Strong CYP3A inhibitors (ketoconazole, itraconazole, clarithromycin, ritonavir, nelfinavir) - contraindicated
moderate: Moderate CYP3A inhibitors (erythromycin, fluconazole, verapamil, diltiazem) - reduce starting dose
ACE inhibitors, ARBs, NSAIDs - increased hyperkalemia
interactions.food: Grapefruit juice may modestly increase exposure; may take with or without food
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction; additive hypotension possible

monitoring: Serum potassium before starting, within first week, at ~1 month, then periodically and after dose/regimen changes
counsel: Get blood tests for potassium and kidney function as scheduled
Avoid potassium supplements and salt substitutes containing potassium unless told otherwise
Report muscle weakness, palpitations, or irregular heartbeat
Do not stop suddenly without medical advice
pk: Antihypertensive effect over days; full effect ~4 weeks
Once-daily dosing supports 24-h effect at steady state
pearls: More selective than spironolactone, so far fewer antiandrogenic effects (gynecomastia, menstrual irregularity).
Metabolized mainly by CYP3A4 - strong CYP3A inhibitors are contraindicated; reduce starting dose with moderate inhibitors.
Hyperkalemia is the dose-limiting toxicity; the dosing-by-potassium table is central to safe titration.
missed: Take the missed dose when remembered the same day; if it is almost time for the next dose, skip it. Do not double up.
overdose: Most likely manifestations are hypotension and hyperkalemia. Treat supportively; manage hyperkalemia with standard measures. Eplerenone is not effectively removed by hemodialysis (high protein binding).
